## Summary

5.2's sofar side is built. crates/sofar-ffi (D53) gives Swift the bodies of `sofar serve`'s /state and /state/<slug>, folded by the Rust core. build-apple.sh assembles an xcframework for macOS (arm64 and x86_64) plus iOS device and simulator, and a SofarCore Swift package; its 4 Swift tests pass against this repo's own record. Testing it surfaced a latent core bug: guards.rs's memoised backtracker hashed every (token, unit) state, which made bench-refresh's 6-pattern `*KEY=*` command guard over 1.4 MB of commands dominate its fold (seen with `sample`; this is a diagnosis, not an npm run perf claim). Replacing it with a bitset Thompson NFA keeps behaviour identical: the old matcher stays as a test reference, with 80k differential cases; CI's conformance, fold-parity, real-logs and render_parity legs all pass. Running conformance.test.ts with SOFAR_CONFORMANCE_BIN produced 27 false golden failures, which were mine, not the change's. 5.2 stays active until desktop-v2 consumes the package.

## Next action

Ship SofarCore to desktop-v2: choose distribution (release-asset xcframework zip + binaryTarget url/checksum, vs a path dependency), then write desktop-v2's CoreFFI RecordSource and add a macOS CI leg for build-apple.sh --test
